RobCo reaches billion-dollar valuation ahead of planned Alfie launch

The transaction combines new investment with an employee secondary sale as RobCo expands US operations and prepares its industrial robot.

Modern Materials Handling ↗5 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Valuation is different from capital raised

RobCo’s valuation exceeded $1 billion in a transaction first reported on October 5 and covered by Modern Materials Handling on October 6. It combines investment in the company with a secondary share sale for employees. The valuation is not a billion-dollar fundraising amount. Participants include existing investors such as Sequoia and Lightspeed and new investors including Cherry Ventures.

Alfie is scheduled for 2027

RobCo plans Alfie’s commercial launch at its RobCoN summit in Munich on March 4, 2027. The company describes an industrial robot combining perception, reasoning and execution for variable factory tasks. That is a product positioning and development goal, not independent proof that it can handle every industrial workflow without preparation.

US operations are expanding

The company reports customer operations across more than a dozen states, manufacturing and assembly in Austin, and a San Francisco lab. CEO Roman Hölzl has relocated to the US. Local operations may support deployment and service, but practical value still depends on application reliability, safety and total costs. The announced commercial launch remains a future milestone.
